messages:
marta: incident-bot fired for streaming p99 spikes across eu-west-1 -> noticed tail stalls on decode path, pages increasing. p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 1.6s -> 4.2s. paging alarm threshold breached :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: latency-slos - channel=#eng-oncall - severity=P2 - alerts=streaming-decode-eu-west-1 - ts=1709998887
sre-bot: autoscaler logs show pending queue growing from 3 -> 18 over last 2m, some nodes in GPU pool entered OOM-kill while kernel module recompiled earlier today
leo: i'm on it, looking at kernel build tags and recent runtimes. last kernel build rolled at 1709990000 with flag -O3 -funsafe-math and new trt8 kernel bundle applied at 1709992000
ashley: customer-impact: a few streaming customers reported slow responses and partial reconnects. support mapping shows 7 tenants with >10% errors in last 10m
marta: UI: streaming endpoints show stalled protobuf frames, logs contain repeated 'kv_cache miss: paging' and 'decode_step blocked on cudaEventSynchronize'
leo: reproducing locally with the trt8+flashattn combo on our test runner, tail latency spikes when sequence length > 1024 and batching mixes with continuous streaming
ashley: notifying account SAs for affected tenants, adding note to status page draft
ops-oncall: can we put a rate limit or slow-path fallback in front of affected model routes to reduce concurrency?
marta: yes, rolling out a temporary per-route concurrency cap to 8 and enabling immediate fallback to cpu-safe-quant model for low-priority requests. doing a canary now on eu-west-1/zone-b
incident-bot: rollout started: route-guard apply --route model-*-stream --concurrency 8 --fallback cpu-quant-v2 - initiated by marta
leo: digging into compile flags: new compile pipeline set FUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1 and ENABLE_TRT_KERNELS=1. if flashattn path doesn't respect our async stream ordering we can get cudaEvent waits that serialize decode
dev-runtime: i can flip the runtime env var to disable flashattn at runtime for the canary. patching configmap and restarting 2 pods in zone-b
ashley: ops team asked for a script to notify customers if mitigation doesn't stabilize in 30m
leo: quick mitigation options (ranked): 1) Disable flashattn kernel at runtime (fast). 2) Revert TRT bundle to previous build (slower, but more authoritative). 3) Rollback kernel build (hotpatch, high risk).
marta: applied runtime disable for flashattn on canary. monitoring...
sre-bot: metric update: canary pods p99 dropped from 3.9s -> 720ms after disabling flashattn; overall region p99 down from 4.2s -> 1.2s but still above SLO
leo: good signal. let's scale canary to 20% of traffic in zone-b then push to remaining zones if stable for 5m
ops-oncall: let's also pin compiler flags for new builds: remove FUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION for now and block new deploys to the pool until we validate
ashley: drafting customer message: "We mitigated elevated latency for streaming in EU-WEST-1 by disabling an experimental kernel optimization. We are continuing to investigate root cause and will update." want review before send
marta: +1. include note that rollback may be required for older TRT bundles if we see regressions after full rollout
leo: collecting decode traces. found stack: 
```
decode_step -> trt_infer_async -> flashattn_forward -> cudaEventSynchronize -> allocate_page -> page_fault -> stall
```
leo: notice memory pressure correlates with spikes; flashattn path temp buffers are larger and we hit kernel page reclaim at higher concurrency
dev-runtime: created quick flag gate: REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION=true in runtime config. patch applied cluster-wide in eu-west-1; restarted 40 pods (graceful).
sre-bot: cluster update metrics: memory pressure normalized in 3m, p95 back to 380ms, p99 ~ 680ms. streaming error rate dropped to baseline
ops-oncall: recommend maintaining the flag until we can produce a validated build that fixes ordering and reduces temp buffer allocations. also recommend a guardrail in our model catalog tagging experimental kernels
leo: next steps: 1) run debug build with extra tracing (allocators + cuda streams) on staging, 2) reproduce with trt8 build + and without, 3) if repro, prepare a TRT rollback candidate and a small kernel hotfix that removes the fusing change causing extra allocations
marta: i'm doing customer comms and monitoring for 30m. will escalate to oncall lead if regression returns
ashley: status page updated: "Mitigation applied: experimental kernel opt disabled. Customers may see improved latency. Investigating root cause."
incident-bot: Incident updated: ID=INC-2024-2247 - mitigation=runtime-flag - severity=P2 - owners=[leo,marta,dev-runtime] - updated_ts=1709999450
leo: starting triage doc in #eng-runtime with trace snippets + heap profiles. tagging @devops for kernel build timeline
dev-runtime: also opened a rollback PR for trt bundle 8.0.1 -> 8.0.0 with validation steps. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/trt-bundles/pull/542
ops-oncall: set CLI guard to block any new kernel compile jobs with FUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION until QA signoff: 
```
ci/guard block --tag FUSE_FLASH_ATTENTION
```
leo: one more data point: p99 for short non-streaming requests unaffected -> indicates issue strongly tied to streaming decode path + KV cache paging interactions
marta: thanks team. leaving a handoff note for night oncall: keep flag disabled, monitor p99 and paging_count metrics, if stable after 1h we can scale down the fallback and plan for scheduled rollback window for TRT
ashley: added postmortem stub to incidents board and assigned to leo for root cause analysis
incident-bot: Pager resolved for now - recovery detected - closed alerts=streaming-decode-eu-west-1 - ts=1709999689
marta: closing thread summary: mitigation=runtime disable of flashattn, root cause suspected=kernel-level fusing change in new TRT bundle increasing temporary buffers -> triggers paging under mixed streaming loads; next=trace+heap R/O, TRT rollback PR validation, postmortem.
